answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, like a sable bond posted before an agent may earn. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a lotus opening petal by petal, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero trust and cannot vote or attest until it has done verifiable work. An attacker who wants many identities must fund every stake and wait through the same slow spiral of earned history, so the cost of faking a crowd grows linearly while an honest agent pays only once.
